title: Mapping the MBE Manuscript to the Package
text: Multi-Component Bayesian Endpoint (MBE) workflow described Lee et al. (2026) two stages: Fit trial-level Bayesian meta-analytic model historical randomized clinical trials. Use draws historical model update treatment effects new trial. package implementation deliberately restricted one clinical endpoint exactly two surrogate endpoints. chronic kidney disease example, two surrogates treatment effects chronic acute eGFR slopes.

title: Mapping the MBE Manuscript to the Package
text: historical dataset either data.table data.frame columns names exactly described .: trial_sim_dat provides shareable simulated example 66 trials. restricted CKD-EPI CT trial data used motivating analysis distributed package.

title: Mapping the MBE Manuscript to the Package
text: historical model can use fixed estimated clinical intercept either half-normal inverse-gamma priors uncertainty parameters. manuscript’s initial specification uses random intercept \beta_0 inverse-gamma priors variance parameters. first simulated trial can held follows: returned object also contains CmdStan fit, posterior draws, sampler diagnostics. Historical fits accepted checking convergence sampler warnings.
code: historical_fields <- c(   "CE_est", "CE_se", "Sur1_est", "Sur1_se", "Sur2_est", "Sur2_se",   "Cor_CE_Sur1", "Cor_CE_Sur2", "Cor_Sur1_Sur2" ) historical_fit <- historical_model_fit_2surrogates(   data = as.data.frame(trial_sim_dat)[-1, historical_fields],   random_intercept = TRUE, #allow for a random intercept. Set to FALSE to fix the intercept at zero.   prior_for_uncertainty = "inverse_gamma", #prior for the variance parameters. If set as "half_normal", then half normal distribution will be modeled on the standard deviation parameters.   nchains = 4, #Number of chains   ncores = 4, #Number of cores for parallel computation. One core per chain is recommended. If set to 1, then all chains will be run sequentially on a single core.   niter = 2000, #Number of post-warmup samples to save for each chain   nwarmup = 1000, #Number of warmup samples to discard for each chain   seed = 2026,   adapt_delta = 0.95,   max_treedepth = 15 )  historical_fit$summary historical_fit$loo historical_fit$waic

title: Mapping the MBE Manuscript to the Package
text: Fitting assessment separate steps. Choose historical-model intercept uncertainty prior, fit model one trial using historical_model_fit_2surrogates(). Repeat held-trial. two assessment functions, loo_cv_rmse() tolerance_interval_coverage(), summarize inputs supplied user; never fit models select priors. internal leave-one-trial-assessment: held-trial serves pseudo-new trial. package uses simulated trials, results expected match manuscript’s CKD trial results.

what: Prepare the fits and point estimates yourself
title: Mapping the MBE Manuscript to the Package
text: following example shows fitting loop explicitly. settings illustrative can changed independently assessment functions. niter number saved post-warmup draws per chain. Run expensive step new fits needed; run building vignette. already fits, reuse posterior draws MBE() calls; need repeat historical fitting step. Saved records earlier development workflow can still read readRDS(path)$posterior_draws. example, original 66 saved records computer, load directly instead running fitting loop:
code: historical_fields <- c(   "CE_est", "CE_se", "Sur1_est", "Sur1_se", "Sur2_est", "Sur2_se",   "Cor_CE_Sur1", "Cor_CE_Sur2", "Cor_Sur1_Sur2" ) trials <- as.data.frame(trial_sim_dat) historical_data <- trials[, historical_fields]  # Your choices for this analysis; the metric functions do not set these. use_random_intercept <- TRUE uncertainty_prior <- "inverse_gamma" use_diffuse_surrogate_prior <- FALSE center_clinical_intercept <- FALSE  paired_effects <- data.frame(   observed = trials$CE_est,   estimated = rep(NA_real_, nrow(trials)),   row.names = as.character(trials$trial_id) ) loo_draws <- vector("list", nrow(trials)) names(loo_draws) <- as.character(trials$trial_id) loo_diagnostics <- vector("list", nrow(trials))  for (i in seq_len(nrow(trials))) {   historical_fit <- historical_model_fit_2surrogates(     data = historical_data[-i, , drop = FALSE],     random_intercept = use_random_intercept,     prior_for_uncertainty = uncertainty_prior,     nchains = 4, ncores = 4, niter = 2000, nwarmup = 1000,     seed = 2026 + i - 1,     adapt_delta = 0.95, max_treedepth = 15   )   loo_draws[[i]] <- historical_fit$posterior_samples   loo_diagnostics[[i]] <- list(     sampler = historical_fit$diagnostics,     convergence = historical_fit$fit$summary()   )    held_out <- list(     ClnEst = trials$CE_est[i], ClnSE = trials$CE_se[i],     Sur1Est = trials$Sur1_est[i], Sur1SE = trials$Sur1_se[i],     Sur2Est = trials$Sur2_est[i], Sur2SE = trials$Sur2_se[i],     R1Clin = trials$Cor_CE_Sur1[i],     R2Clin = trials$Cor_CE_Sur2[i], R12 = trials$Cor_Sur1_Sur2[i]   )   set.seed(2026 + i - 1)   updated <- MBE(     mcmc_dat = loo_draws[[i]], sample_dat = held_out,     diffuse = use_diffuse_surrogate_prior,     intercept0 = center_clinical_intercept   )   paired_effects$estimated[i] <- updated$post_mean[1, 1] }  # Inspect diagnostics and resolve fitting issues before interpreting the metric. loo_diagnostics[[1]] loo_cv_rmse(paired_effects) trials <- as.data.frame(trial_sim_dat) loo_draws <- lapply(as.character(trials$trial_id), function(id) {   record <- readRDS(file.path(     "data-raw/loo-random-inverse-gamma", paste0("heldout_trial_", id, ".rds")   ))   stopifnot(identical(as.character(record$held_out_trial), id))   record$posterior_draws }) names(loo_draws) <- as.character(trials$trial_id) use_diffuse_surrogate_prior <- FALSE center_clinical_intercept <- FALSE

what: Calculate RMSE from a two-column table
title: Mapping the MBE Manuscript to the Package
text: Supply one row per trial two columns named observed estimated. data frame numeric matrix accepted, columns either order. Match trial IDs assembling pairs. estimate chosen user; example uses posterior mean MBE(), estimate true effect rather known true effect. calculation sqrt(mean((observed - estimated)^2)). full MBE update, held-clinical estimate contributes posterior mean. measures agreement updating, rather prediction surrogates alone. Calling metric LOO-CV assumes corresponding trial excluded historical fitting; metric function verify step.
code: data("loo_assessment_by_trial", package = "MBE") paired_effects <- data.frame(   observed = loo_assessment_by_trial$observed_clinical,   estimated = loo_assessment_by_trial$posterior_mean_clinical ) loo_cv_rmse(paired_effects) #> [1] 0.2385382 loo_cv_rmse(as.matrix(paired_effects)) #> [1] 0.2385382

what: Generate the clinical predictive distribution and check capture
title: Mapping the MBE Manuscript to the Package
text: clinical_predictive_distribution() takes historical posterior draws held-trial’s surrogate estimates, standard errors, sampling correlations. generates draws observed clinical estimate conditional two surrogate estimates. clinical estimate ignored even ClnEst present input list. example reuses historical_posterior new_trial ; trial 1 excluded historical fit: tolerance_interval_coverage() calls prediction function internally. Supply desired lower upper quantile probabilities: c(0.025, 0.975) 95% interval, one row per interval two-column matrix. Asymmetric intervals also supported. result one row per probability pair: lower_prob, upper_prob, level (percentage), observed, lower, upper, logical covered. Bounds use stats::quantile(type = 7), endpoints count covered. function generates predictive draws per trial, uses draws requested intervals. fixed seed makes simulation reproducible. multiple trials, reuse loo_draws list fitting example, match trial IDs, combine single-trial results: Prediction conditions joint observed-effect distribution two surrogate estimates. incorporates residual clinical heterogeneity, clinical sampling variance, surrogate uncertainty, supplied sampling correlations. Historical draws weighted likelihood observed surrogates. different passing latent-effect draws MBE()$post_psi0, already condition observed clinical estimate.
code: predictive_draws <- clinical_predictive_distribution(   mcmc_dat = historical_posterior, sample_dat = new_trial,   diffuse = FALSE, intercept0 = FALSE,   n_draws = 4000, seed = 2026 ) stats::quantile(predictive_draws, c(0.025, 0.975)) #>       2.5%      97.5%  #> -0.3745658  0.1562384 interval_probs <- rbind(   c(0.025, 0.975),  # 95%   c(0.05, 0.95),    # 90%   c(0.075, 0.925)   # 85% ) tolerance_interval_coverage(   observed = new_trial$ClnEst,   mcmc_dat = historical_posterior, sample_dat = new_trial,   probs = interval_probs,   diffuse = FALSE, intercept0 = FALSE,   n_draws = 4000, seed = 2026 ) #>   lower_prob upper_prob level   observed      lower      upper covered #> 1      0.025      0.975    95 -0.1337531 -0.3745658 0.15623836    TRUE #> 2      0.050      0.950    90 -0.1337531 -0.3326389 0.10673561    TRUE #> 3      0.075      0.925    85 -0.1337531 -0.3078896 0.07480282    TRUE stopifnot(   !is.null(names(loo_draws)), !anyDuplicated(names(loo_draws)),   !anyDuplicated(trials$trial_id),   setequal(as.character(trials$trial_id), names(loo_draws)) ) loo_draws <- loo_draws[as.character(trials$trial_id)] capture <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(trials)), function(i) {   held_out <- list(     ClnSE = trials$CE_se[i],     Sur1Est = trials$Sur1_est[i], Sur1SE = trials$Sur1_se[i],     Sur2Est = trials$Sur2_est[i], Sur2SE = trials$Sur2_se[i],     R1Clin = trials$Cor_CE_Sur1[i],     R2Clin = trials$Cor_CE_Sur2[i], R12 = trials$Cor_Sur1_Sur2[i]   )   result <- tolerance_interval_coverage(     observed = trials$CE_est[i],     mcmc_dat = loo_draws[[i]], sample_dat = held_out,     probs = interval_probs, n_draws = 8000, seed = 2026 + i - 1,     diffuse = use_diffuse_surrogate_prior,     intercept0 = center_clinical_intercept   )   data.frame(trial_id = trials$trial_id[i], result) })) stats::aggregate(covered ~ lower_prob + upper_prob, data = capture, FUN = mean)

what: Multi-Component Bayesian Endpoints with Two Surrogates
title: Multi-Component Bayesian Endpoints with Two Surrogates
text: repository contains R package accompanying Multi-Component Bayesian Endpoints Randomized Clinical Trials manuscript Lee et al. (2026). package implements MBE exactly one clinical endpoint two surrogate endpoints. current CKD implementation uses chronic acute eGFR slopes two surrogates. Bayesian framework incorporates historical randomized clinical trials (RCTs) propagates uncertainty estimating treatment effect clinical endpoint surrogate effects. See Mapping MBE Manuscript Package complete workflow.

title: Multi-Component Bayesian Endpoints with Two Surrogates

title: Estimate an MBE Posterior with Two Surrogate Endpoints — MBE
text: mcmc_dat data frame matrix containing posterior draws two-surrogate historical model. sample_dat named list containing exactly nine scalar values: ClnEst, ClnSE, Sur1Est, Sur1SE, Sur2Est, Sur2SE, R1Clin, R2Clin, R12. diffuse logical value indicating whether use diffuse prior. Defaults TRUE. diffuse_se positive numeric value specifying standard deviation diffuse prior two surrogate effects. intercept0 logical value indicating whether center intercept term meta-regression zero. Defaults TRUE.

title: Estimate an MBE Posterior with Two Surrogate Endpoints — MBE
text: list containing posterior means, posterior covariance, weighted quantiles clinical two surrogate effects, posterior draws, corresponding importance weights, importance-sampling diagnostics. diagnostic vector reports effective sample size, effective sample size relative number historical draws, maximum normalized weight. Endpoint components always ordered clinical endpoint, surrogate 1, surrogate 2.

title: Estimate an MBE Posterior with Two Surrogate Endpoints — MBE
code: # Use the example data provided in the package. # Load the historical posterior samples where the model was fit # with random intercept and inverse gamma prior for variance parameters # on the 65/66 simulated trials in `trial_sim_dat` dataset. # It's the first trial that was left out as if it was a new trial. # We demonstrate estimating the posterior distribution of MBE on this first # row that was left out. data("historical_posterior") data("trial_sim_dat") one_sim_dat<-list(  # treatment effect on CE ClnEst=trial_sim_dat$CE_est[1], ClnSE=trial_sim_dat$CE_se[1],  # treatment effect on chronic slope Sur1Est=trial_sim_dat$Sur1_est[1], Sur1SE=trial_sim_dat$Sur1_se[1],  # treatment effect on acute slope Sur2Est=trial_sim_dat$Sur2_est[1], Sur2SE=trial_sim_dat$Sur2_se[1],  # correlation between CE and chronic slope R1Clin=trial_sim_dat$Cor_CE_Sur1[1],  # correlation between CE and acute slope R2Clin=trial_sim_dat$Cor_CE_Sur2[1],  # correlation between chronic slope and acute slope R12=trial_sim_dat$Cor_Sur1_Sur2[1] )  MBE_distribution<-MBE( mcmc_dat = historical_posterior, sample_dat=one_sim_dat, diffuse_se = 100, diffuse = TRUE, intercept0 = TRUE )  head(MBE_distribution$post_psi0) #>         clinical surrogate1 surrogate2 #> [1,] -0.01742418  0.4358344  -7.647448 #> [2,] -0.05070114  0.3625249  -5.290546 #> [3,] -0.21549799  0.9284195  -4.653444 #> [4,] -0.22270912  1.0586468  -4.846612 #> [5,] -0.02885444  0.6432777  -8.217527 #> [6,] -0.22661395  0.9851503  -4.977536

title: Fit the Historical Model for Exactly Two Surrogate Endpoints — historical_model_fit_2surrogates
text: function fits trial-level meta-analysis model using 2-stage random effects Bayesian model chronic kidney disease (CKD) context first introduced Lee et al. (2026). true treatment effect clinical endpoint \(\theta_i\), true treatment effect two surrogate endpoints \(\gamma_{, 1}\) \(\gamma_{, 2}\) \(\)-th trial, model specified follows: $$\hat{\psi}_i \mid \psi_i \sim N_3(\psi_i, \Sigma_{y, })$$ \(\psi_i = (\theta_i, \gamma_{, 1}, \gamma_{, 2})^T\) true treatment effect vector \(\)-th trial, \(\hat{\psi}_i\) observed (estimated) treatment effect vector \(\)-th trial, \(\Sigma_{y, }\) covariance matrix corresponding \(\hat{\psi}_i\). density \(\psi\) can expressed sequence conditional densities: $$\gamma_{, 2} \sim N(\mu_2, \sigma_2^2)$$ $$\gamma_{, 1} \mid \gamma_{, 2} \sim N(\alpha_{\gamma_1} + \beta_{\gamma_1} \cdot \gamma_{, 2}, \lambda^2_{\gamma_1})$$ $$\theta_i \mid \gamma_{, 1}, \gamma_{, 2} \sim N(\alpha_\theta + \beta_{\gamma_1} \cdot \gamma_{, 1} + \beta_{\gamma_2} \cdot \gamma_{, 2}, \lambda^2_\theta)$$ function fits model using MCMC sampling historical RCTs returns posterior distribution model parameters. loo waic components conditional model-fit measures based manuscript's Stan log-likelihood. distinct explicit internal leave-one-trial-assessment. assessment, call fitting function separately set training trials, omitting held-trial. use loo_cv_rmse() paired effects tolerance_interval_coverage() already fitted posterior draws held-sampling inputs. latter calls clinical_predictive_distribution(). assessment functions fit models choose priors.

Instead, we will use a diffuse prior. diffuse_se = 100, intercept0 = FALSE)
